title: oysterlsp.json
description: Configuration for the Oystermark language server, read from oysterlsp.json at the vault root. Every setting also has an initializationOptions equivalent, which this file overrides key by key. Anything unusable falls back to the default and is reported at startup rather than failing.

$schema.description: Association to this schema, so an editor's JSON language server offers completion and validation here. Not a setting.

disable.description: Turn the server off for this vault. It still starts — a client spawns it and this file is only read afterwards — but it indexes nothing and answers every request emptily, saying so once at startup. Every other setting in this file is then irrelevant, and warnings about them are suppressed.

dailyNotes.description: Where daily notes live and how they are named. See the daily-notes feature spec.

format.description: Date format naming the note, as a subset of the moment.js tokens (YYYY, MM, DD, MMM, MMMM, ddd, dddd, and [literal] text). May contain '/' to nest notes in folders. An unsupported format disables the daily-note actions entirely and is reported at startup.

folder.description: Vault-relative folder the daily notes live under. Omit for the vault root.

template.description: Stubbed: the setting round-trips but note creation always makes an empty note.

linkAction.description: Whether to offer the 'Insert link to today's daily note' code action. It is the only daily-note action offered in every menu in the vault, and the only one that reaches its note without window/showDocument — so turning it off in a client lacking that capability gives up reaching daily notes altogether.

maxChars.description: Bytes of note content a hover may include, excluding the path header. Content past the limit is truncated at the previous newline, followed by a notice reporting how much is shown, e.g. '*(truncated: showing 42 of 80 lines, 52%)*'. Does not apply to image hovers.

imagePreview.description: Whether hovering an image link embeds the image itself as a data: URI, after the description line naming its format, dimensions and size. Off by default because rendering it is the client's markdown renderer's business: VS Code shows the picture, a client that lays hover markdown out as text (Neovim's built-in handler, most terminal clients) shows nothing. The description is shown either way.

imageMaxBytes.description: Largest image imagePreview will embed, measured on the file before base64 inflates it by a third. The encoded image travels inline in the JSON-RPC response the editor is blocking a hover on. A larger file keeps its description and says why the preview is missing.

linkDirection.description: Whether to show a direction arrow and line distance after each link whose target is in the same note, e.g. '[[#setup]]↓8'. Independent of the inbound-reference counts shown at headings.

references.description: Whether to show a '3 references' lens above each heading something links to, and a '12 backlinks' lens above the note. Note that clients gate code lens themselves — Zed's 'code_lens' setting is off by default.

countTocLinks.description: Whether links inside a '::: toc' region count towards the lens. Off by default: the server wrote those links, and counting them puts a lens above every heading of every note that has a table of contents. On, they are counted as links the note makes to itself.

showReferencesCommand.description: The client-side command a reference lens carries, invoked with [uri, position, locations]. There is no standard LSP command for 'show me these locations' — this name is VS Code's convention, which Zed also implements — so it is a setting rather than a constant. Set it to "" to make the lens a label with nothing behind it.

unresolvedFragment.description: What to do with a link whose file exists but whose heading or block-id fragment does not. 'fallback' jumps to the top of the file; 'strict' returns no result.
What to do with a link whose file exists but whose fragment does not. 'fallback' warns about nothing; 'strict' reports the fragment as unresolved.
